context:
Use this bundled corpus (week-01), written out in full below; it is the only data. Each report has an id, a UTC publication time, a source (irrelevant), and its text. The corpus is already in publication order (by published time, then id).

Compute every pair of reports (earlier report first, later report second). For each pair:
- words: maximal runs of letters or digits in the lower-cased text, so '104-97' contributes the two words '104' and '97'; punctuation and spaces separate words.
- shingles of size 3: the set of all runs of 3 consecutive words; because it is a set, a repeated shingle in one report counts once.
- similarity_percent: 100 * |intersection| / |union| of the two shingle sets, truncated (never rounded) to 4 decimal places.
- same_numbers: true iff the two texts have exactly the same set of runs of digits; a changed score, stat or date makes it false.

A pair is a near-duplicate iff similarity_percent is at least 75 (compared as given: 75.0 qualifies, 74.9999 does not) AND same_numbers is true. A report is redundant iff it is the later report of at least one near-duplicate pair; its duplicate_of is the id of the earliest such earlier report in publication order, and its similarity_percent is that pair's truncated value exactly, never rounded. Every other report is kept. Output the redundant entries in publication order of the redundant report, then the kept ids in publication order of the kept reports; every report appears exactly once.
